fused_decoder.reason: the fused rewrites (tt/fused_decoder.py, FusedFlags) replace op sequences inside a step; they add no state, keep the paged DSA latent / pool-key caches, the KDA recurrent / conv state and the page-table contract of the functional decoder, and every row-count-dependent path (head ops at prefill rows > 32, indexer row blocks, mhc_mix chunks) is defined for any row count

full_model.dsa_cache: paged shared pool of 128-token blocks, replicated per die, 11,968 B per token; KDA state 35.65 MB per slot per die
full_model.dram_budget_note: E192 weights at bfp4 experts are ~28.5 GiB of the 31.9 GiB per die; the 11 DSA layers' latent cache (512 x 2 B per token per layer) and the 34 KDA states per slot share the remainder. Any reduction below the advertised context will be recorded here with the byte calculation and a capacity probe.

multichip_decoder.hardware: p300x2, mesh (1, 4), FABRIC_1D, TP4 (tt/multichip_decoder.py; stage-4 path MCOpts(), code default DEFAULT_MC)

dsa_cache_layouts.block-sharded (MCOpts.dsa_shard / GLM53_: global block b on die b % 4 (local block b // 4), rows 544 wide (latent + 32 control columns); pool keys, indexer and selection replicated: 11 x (544 x 2 / 4 + 64) = 3,696 B per token per die

per_die.kda_state_note: 34 layers x 16 local heads x 128 x 128 fp32; max_batch 1 holds 2 slots (padding slot, MultichipKDA)

capability_reduction.reason: device DRAM per die after weights (32.13 GB of 34.11 GB allocatable). Block-sharded is the largest measured layout; 1,048,576 tokens need 3.9 GB of DSA cache per die even sharded (3,696 B x 1M) vs ~1.25 GB available. Further steps (memory_budget.json path_to_1M): shard the pool keys too (2,992 B), a bfp8 / fp8 latent, host embedding lookup.

optimized_multichip_decoder.hardware: p300x2, mesh (1, 4), FABRIC_1D, TP4 (tt/multichip_decoder.py, MCOpts / DEFAULT_MC)

per_die_state_bytes.dsa_cache_note: replicated on every die: 11 DSA layers x (latent 512 x 2 B + pooled index key 128 x 2 B / 4)
per_die_state_bytes.kda_state_per_slot: 1 MiB recurrent state (16 local heads) + conv history per KDA layer per die
per_die_state_bytes.one_slot_padding: max_batch = 1: KDA kda.recurrent_decode needs batch x 16 heads % 32 == 0, so a 1-slot decoder allocates 2 KDA state slots: +1 MiB per KDA layer per die (34 MiB per die, ~2.9K tokens of DSA cache)
per_die_state_bytes.collective_buffers: none persistent: ag_persistent is rejected (it broke the 45-layer model); decode collective outputs are per-call L1 tensors
per_die_state_bytes.review2_constants: dsa_q_mm head mask [32, 4096] bf16 (0.25 MB), one per mesh shared by all DSA layers (W_UK is a view); one dsa_tail_shared sparse-index tail tile [1, 1, S, 32] fp32 per model, allocated when the first DSA layer is built

optimized_multichip_decoder.weights: unchanged: both DSA packs are concatenations of the separate weights (ds_shared frees those), the 1D decode programs read the same interleaved weights
optimized_multichip_decoder.supported_context: full_model.supported_context (measured 1-slot limit 104,448 tokens with this decoder's state; per-slot profiles there)
optimized_multichip_decoder.cache_dtype_candidates: bfp8 latent impossible: sparse_sdpa takes ROW_MAJOR bf16 or FP8_E4M3 KV only (bfp8 is a tile format). FP8_E4M3 halves the latent (3 mantissa bits) but needs both scatter_rows write paths cast to FP8 and a model-accuracy check: stage-8 datatype-sweep item. The path to the advertised 1,048,576 is the sequence-sharded latent (stage-4 rework: MCOpts.dsa_shard).
optimized_multichip_decoder.status: unchanged from the multichip decoder (see multichip_decoder; the block-sharded DSA cache is an MCOpts option of both)
